words.gloss: if they are able to see

literal: If they are able to see their own fault like strangers' fault, is there evil to the enduring soul?
translation: If people could look at their own faults in the same way they look at the faults of strangers, is there any harm that can ever come to their enduring lives?
modern: அயலாரின் குற்றத்தைக் காண்பது போலத் தம்முடைய குற்றத்தையும் காண வல்லவரானால், நிலைபெற்று வாழும் உயிர்க்கு ஏதேனும் துன்பம் உண்டோ?
explanation: This couplet addresses the human tendency to judge others while ignoring one's own flaws. The poet suggests that if we could examine our own faults with the same critical eye we use for strangers, we would naturally correct ourselves. By focusing on self-improvement rather than backbiting, we protect ourselves from harm. Consequently, no evil can ever affect a life that is guided by such self-awareness.
